title: Email Pipeline & Submission Dashboard
text: Live

title: Email Pipeline & Submission Dashboard
text:
The problem
Weekly submission statistics depended on a VBA macro built in 2014 that downloaded one email per second, ran once a week, and locked the computer while it worked. Parsing email titles into fields produced wrong and missing values, so every run was followed by manual edits. The volume: around 500 submissions per week, on top of an archive of roughly 120,000 emails.

  BeforeAfter
  
    
    
  
  After · the live submission dashboard

title: Email Pipeline & Submission Dashboard
text:
The new script

  ★The core of the rebuild
  A Python tool that does in 30 seconds what used to take an hour
  A small application with a GUI: pick the Outlook folder, pick the mode, run. It finds the right emails, normalises every date format, and applies 57 regex patterns to pull clean fields out of inconsistent titles. The patterns are ordered from most specific to most general, so the messy real-world cases are caught first.

Here is the heart of the parser, the ordered pattern list that replaced years of manual correction:

  Part of the 57-pattern parser, ordered most specific first
  The GUI: pick a folder, pick a mode, run

The script can run automatically on computer start or manually for double checks, so the data is daily by default instead of weekly by ritual. It writes a clean CSV rather than Excel, which handles the 120,000-email archive without strain.

title: Email Pipeline & Submission Dashboard
text:
The Power BI rebuild
The clean CSV feeds a rebuilt Power BI model, not a pile of pivot tables. The new structure uses organised folders and subfolders, dynamic measures written as DAX rather than copied cells, and a clean, deduplicated data model connected through SharePoint. It is a proper star schema: a central fact table of emails joined to dimension tables for date and category, so the dynamic graphs adapt to the latest weeks on their own.

  Measures in organised folders, not scattered
  Named measure groups and conformed tables
  Star schema: fact table joined to dimensions

title: Email Pipeline & Submission Dashboard
text:
Outcome
Around 5 hours saved every week, plus the manual checks and corrections that no longer exist. The team now has consistent, clean data since 2019 and a dashboard that is always current. All documentation lives in QMD files rendered to HTML.

  A page from the live dashboard
  The old data: highlighted and patched by hand

title: Email Pipeline & Submission Dashboard
text:
Before and after

  BeforeA 2014 VBA macro crawling Outlook at one email per second, run once a week, freezing the machine and mangling half the fields it parsed.
  AfterA background Python tool with 57 regex patterns, a clean CSV archive of 120,000 emails, and a live dashboard that needs no manual refresh.My touch: I designed the parser around the messiest real titles first, not the clean ones, so the patterns hold against what people actually send.

title: Revenue & Expenditure Pipeline
text:
The problem
Revenue and expenditure reporting depended on more than 20 separate SAP reports, each extracted by hand as an Excel file. Filters were applied inside individual workbooks and could not be traced afterwards. Data structures differed between teams, so Finance, Procurement and others routinely produced numbers that disagreed with each other.

  BeforeAfter
  
    
    
  
  After · the live governed dashboard

title: Revenue & Expenditure Pipeline
text:
What I built
I helped rewrite most of the data ingestion around one idea: a live connection instead of file exports. Working with SAP consultants, we moved the source layer to SAP Datasphere and rebuilt the data model there, so every filter and field is defined once rather than inside someone’s workbook. A live gateway then feeds Power BI directly.

The new model is a clean star schema: a small set of fact tables (revenue, expenditure, commitments) connected to shared dimension tables for date, entity, fund and category. Measures sit in organised display folders rather than scattered across reports, and the data is deduplicated at the source. The result is year-to-date (YTD) data refreshed daily, with more than 20 report views rebuilt on one foundation.

  THE NEW DATA FLOW
  SAP Datasphere (governed model, deduplicated)  →  live gateway  →  Power BI  →  YTD data, refreshed daily, 20+ views.

title: Revenue & Expenditure Pipeline
text:
The data model
A blurred view of the rebuilt model. Fact tables sit at the centre, connected to conformed dimension tables, the structure that replaced 20-plus disconnected extracts.

  Star schema: fact tables connected to shared dimensions

title: Revenue & Expenditure Pipeline
text:
Outcome
Refresh frequency went from monthly or quarterly (and different per team) to daily for the whole organisation. The change saved around 40 collective working hours per week across the teams involved in reporting, and resolved more than 300 inconsistencies between reporting mechanisms and incorrect values.

  One of the rebuilt report views
  The kind of manual report it replaced

title: Revenue & Expenditure Pipeline
text:
Before and after

  BeforeTwenty-plus reports pulled from SAP by hand every cycle, each one filtered inside its own workbook, none of them agreeing with the next.
  AfterOne governed model in SAP Datasphere feeding Power BI live. Same definitions for every team, refreshed daily, traceable end to end.My touch: the real win was getting Finance and Procurement to agree on one definition of every field before a single line of the model was written.

title: About
text:
Open to interesting problems
I am a financial and data engineer. My background is finance and portfolio management (MSc, University of Rome Tor Vergata), and my day to day is making financial data flow without human glue: SQL pipelines, Python tooling, Power BI, and lately agentic AI systems that I keep on a short leash.

title: About
text:
How I work

  01Map priorities, build for the teamEvery tool starts as something done by hand. I map what matters first, then build around how the team actually works, not how I would prefer it to work.
  02The interface should help the userA tool is only as good as its adoption. The interface has to carry the user through the task, so the right action is the easy one and mistakes are hard to make.
  03Document or it does not existA tool nobody else can run is a liability. Everything I build ships with rendered documentation and a guide, so it survives me being away.

text: Live and active

title: Invoice Reconciliation Tool
text:
The problem
Checking supplier invoices meant combining 5 separate SAP extracts against a reference table in a static shared database, where each person uploaded and downloaded the latest version. Across several teams this turned into chaos: constant reminders, emails back and forth, and no certainty about which file was current. Each cycle covered more than 200 invoices and disputes, some open for years, across many procedure types.

  BeforeAfter
  
    
    
  
  After · one validated master file

title: Invoice Reconciliation Tool
text:
The new script

  ★The tool that ended the email chains
  Drop five files in a folder, run, get one source of truth
  A fully automated script packaged as a standalone EXE, so the team runs it without installing Python. It validates the file formats, extracts the data, applies all matching, transformation, checking and deduplication rules, archives the input files with timestamps, writes a run log, and produces a master CSV holding the full archive. On top of that sits an Excel view with colour-coded checks and an embedded summary table, because the people reading it live in Excel.


  The standalone EXE: no Python needed
  Part of the matching and deduplication logic
  The clean drop-in folder structure

title: Invoice Reconciliation Tool
text:
The data model
Behind the Excel view sits a clean, deduplicated model: a fact table of invoices and disputes joined to dimension tables for supplier, procedure type and status. The same structured approach that makes the dashboards trustworthy.

  Fact table joined to supplier, procedure and status dimensions

title: Invoice Reconciliation Tool
text:
Outcome
A single source of truth where there used to be five files and an argument. Around 10 hours of weekly work saved, plus the removal of manual checks that regularly produced wrong results. The script processes all extracts simultaneously and writes thousands of rows to the master file in seconds.

  The auto-generated, colour-coded Excel summary
  The manual reconciliation it replaced

title: Invoice Reconciliation Tool
text:
Before and after

  BeforeFive SAP extracts merged by hand against a shared static file, passed around by email, with no certainty which version was current.
  AfterDrop the files in a folder, run the EXE, get one validated master file with colour-coded checks and a full audit log.My touch: I shipped it as an EXE so nobody had to install Python. Adoption was instant because the tool asked nothing of the people using it.

Stack: Python (packaged EXE), data matching and deduplication, CSV master file, Excel reporting layer

title: Living Documentation System
text:
The problem
Team documentation lived in Word files full of pasted screenshots and links that broke over time. Versions diverged across teams, changes were untracked, and every update meant manual fixes throughout the document, with mismatched fonts, oversized logos, and highlights in every colour.

  BeforeAfter
  
    
    
  
  After · one rendered, templated HTML document

title: Living Documentation System
text:
What I built

  ★One template, every document
  A documentation system built on Quarto and Markdown
  Documents are written in Markdown inside a shared QMD template, with a single YAML header controlling everything: the title banner, the table of contents, syntax highlighting, and output to both HTML and PDF from the same source. One style.css carries the house colours, so every output looks identical regardless of who wrote it.

The result is interactive rather than static: a live table of contents, collapsable callout boxes, cross references between documents, and images and graphs that update with the underlying data instead of being pasted in. Links stay alive because they are part of the build, not copied by hand.

title: Living Documentation System
text:
Why it matters
This is the quiet backbone of everything else here. Every tool I ship comes documented in this format, so it survives me being on holiday. The same YAML produces a clean web page for quick reference and a PDF for formal sign-off, from one file, with no reformatting.

  The rendered HTML: TOC, banner, callouts, styled code
  The Word file it replaced

title: Living Documentation System
text:
Outcome
Interconnected, linkable documents that can be reproduced in the same format every time. Managers get consistent reporting; the team gets documentation that is actually current. Video guides complement the written docs for onboarding.

title: Living Documentation System
text:
Before and after

  BeforeWord documents full of pasted screenshots and links that broke over time, with versions quietly drifting apart across teams.
  AfterOne QMD template and one stylesheet rendering to interconnected HTML and PDF, with a live table of contents and cross references that never rot.My touch: one YAML header produces both the web page and the formal PDF, so there is never a second version to keep in sync.
  click to reveal

Stack: Quarto (QMD, Markdown), YAML, HTML, CSS, PDF output, video editing for guides
